subject: [PATCH 42/46] mm/huge_memory: split huge PUDs when adjusting VMA boundaries

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David pointed out that __split_huge_pud() must split a leaf PUD, either by zapping it or populating page tables, and suggested adding a WARN_ON_ONCE check to ensure pud_leaf(pud) is true before attempting the split.
reviews.raw_body:
__split_huge_pud() must split a leave. Either by zapping it (what we do right
now) or by populating page tables (as in Usama's PoC).

We can throw in here a

	if (WARN_ON_ONCE(!pud_leaf(pud)))
		return;

But I don't see how that would be required.

If we run into an un-splittable PUD something else is completely messed up.

(this is not hugetlb code :) )

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: Author clarified that the issue arises when pud_leaf() is true but split_pud is false, causing __split_huge_pud() to be skipped despite pud_present() being true.
reviews.raw_body:
No, meant the situation when pud_leaf() is true, but split_pud is false,
so __split_huge_pud() is never hit. pud_present() is true so we proceed
to pmd_offset()

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the patch incorrectly handles PUDs that were already leaf nodes, and suggested adding a WARN_ON_ONCE() to indicate this bug in software
reviews.raw_body:
Oh, yeah, I can add a WARN_ON_ONCE() for that, it would be a bug in the software.

I was a bit careful in pud_split_required() to not harm performance of things
that don't need a split because pud leaves (should be) are impossible.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David (Arm) noted that the split_pud check is unnecessary and suggested dropping it to simplify the code.

2026-10-29.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the truncate operation in the Linux kernel by reducing the number of lookups required when a folio is left behind in the mapping. Normally, two lookups are performed: one from the start and one from the end of the range. However, if the second loop had work to do, it means that there's still something left in the mapping, so instead of performing another lookup from the start, the patch reuses the existing loop that goes back to the start when necessary. This reduces the number of lookups required and improves performance.
